root_cause.text: The MCTP netlink response handlers in device.c, neigh.c, and route.c failed to zero-initialize the entire netlink message header structure before populating specific fields, resulting in uninitialized padding bytes being leaked to userspace.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `memset(hdr, 0, sizeof(*hdr))` calls in `mctp_fill_addrinfo`, `mctp_fill_neigh`, and `mctp_fill_rtinfo` to ensure netlink data is initialized to zero, fixing the CVE report that RTM_GETNEIGH returned uninitialized data in the pad bytes of the ndmsg data.

vuln_statements.explanation: The nlmsghdr pointer was declared but not zero-initialized before use in the netlink response handler, causing uninitialized padding bytes to be leaked to userspace when the message was sent.
Similar to device.c, the neigh.c handler failed to zero-initialize the nlmsghdr structure before populating fields, allowing kernel memory contents to leak via padding bytes.
The route.c netlink response handler had the same vulnerability pattern - nlmsghdr was used without memset() or zero-initialization, resulting in uninitialized memory exposure.
